question: How do I apply to the College of Engineering?
reference: Start by applying to the University of Utah; the college's admission requirements are the same as the university's. See [How to Apply](https://www.price.utah.edu/future/admissions).

question: Are the engineering admission requirements different from the rest of the U?
reference: No. The college's admission requirements for freshman and transfer students are the same as the University of Utah's.

question: Do I need to be ready for calculus when I start engineering?
reference: Being ready for Calculus I is helpful but not necessary; first-year engineering students are expected to complete calculus in their first year.

question: When is the next engineering info session?
reference: The next virtual information session is November 20, 2026, then January 27 and April 16, 2027.
notes: Info sessions are listed on the page, not on the Trumba calendar.

question: Can I tour the engineering side of campus?
reference: Yes. Price College tours with a current student or staff member run Monday through Friday.

question: When are the transfer student information sessions?
reference: The Transfer Students page lists virtual sessions on September 13, October 19 and November 10, but it was last updated in October 2024, so confirm current dates with the college.
notes: Stale-content trap: the page lists dates with no year and was last updated Oct 2024. A good answer flags that.

question: What engineering majors can I study?
reference: Majors include Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Electrical & Computer, Materials Science and Mechanical Engineering, plus Computer Science. See [Majors and Minors](https://www.price.utah.edu/majors-in-engineering).

question: Does the college offer minors or certificates?
reference: Yes. The Majors and Minors page lists the college's minors and certificates alongside its majors.

question: Where can I get tutoring help for my engineering classes?
reference: Each department runs a tutoring program alongside TA office hours; check Canvas and your syllabus for TA hours, and ask your academic advisor for more support.

question: How do I petition to withdraw from a class after the deadline?
reference: Price College students use the Petitions process; step one is meeting with your academic advisor.

question: What is the CLEAR program?
reference: CLEAR (Communication, Leadership, Ethics and Research) helps engineering undergraduates build communication, teamwork and ethics skills.

question: Is there engineering student housing, and how do I sign up?
reference: The Engineering Floor is in Kahlert Village and Kennecott House. Apply at housing.utah.edu, choose the Living and Learning option, and pick the Engineering Floor first.

question: How can I become a Price College engineering ambassador?
reference: You need to be an enrolled, degree-seeking Price College student in good academic standing; applications open again in early December.

question: What are the college's research priority areas?
reference: They include Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace, AI & Machine Learning, Biomedical & Neurotech, Energy Systems, Robotics & Autonomous Systems, Semiconductors and more.

question: Does the college have a center that helps people develop medical device ideas?
reference: Yes, the Center for Medical Innovation (CMI) supports innovators from ideation through prototyping and business planning.

question: Can I watch the construction of the new Price Computing and Engineering Building?
reference: Yes, there's a live construction feed for the John and Marcia Price Computing and Engineering Building.

question: What would my schedule look like for CS if I followed a 4.5 year track?
reference: The CS 4.5-year plan (CS handbook 2024-2025) starts Track A with CS 1420, Calculus I and two Gen Eds; confirm with a CS academic advisor.
notes: Freshman fall in Track A is CS 1420, MATH 1210 and two Gen Eds (28-credit year); CS 2100 is sophomore fall.

question: Should I start with CS 1400 or CS 1420?
reference: CS 1400 then CS 1410 is the most common path at a comfortable pace; CS 1420 is an accelerated course for students with programming experience.

question: How many credits does the biomedical engineering degree take?
reference: The BME B.S. requires a minimum of 127 semester hours (BME Undergraduate Handbook 2026/27).

question: What classes would I take my first semester in civil engineering?
reference: The 2026-2027 civil flowchart's first fall includes CVEEN 1000 Intro to Civil & Environmental Engineering, a math course and writing; confirm with an advisor.

question: What do I need to get full major status in computer science?
reference: Finish the pre-major courses (CS 1400/1410 or 1420, CS 2420, Calculus I and II); CS 2420 needs a B- or above and Calculus I a C or above (CS handbook 2024-2025).

question: How many times can I retake a CS class?
reference: Any course may be taken at most twice, and any grade including a W counts as an attempt; two unsuccessful attempts result in probation (CS handbook 2024-2025).
